5) Nest was Destroyed and we drew Queen Token during bag development — Surely you can't still place an egg? We played it as nothing happened, almost like a blank token draw when you have no adult tokens left to add.

The Nest being "destroyed" is somewhat poorly defined. I don't think we have a clear answer to your question without a developer chiming in.

6) Can you use room actions like Send the Signal while in combat? It seems thematically like you could not, but I did not find a rule on this and the room actions did not have the icon that you find on non-combat cards.

I've seen people say you can't use room actions in combat, and I do think it's the intent, but the rules are poorly written here. Room actions probably should have the "out of combat" symbol on them and I suggest playing as such.

I will quote directly from the Rulebook:
"Whenever your Character is in a Room with any uncarried Eggs (not carried by any Character), you can try to destroy these Eggs. Resolve this Action as a Shoot Action or Melee Attack Action. Each Injury (of any type) destroys 1 Egg.
In the case of a Melee Attack Action, the Character does not draw a Contamination card or suffer Wounds if they miss.
You can also throw grenades into a Room with uncarried Eggs as if an Intruder were there. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs, a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1 Egg.
After every single attempt to destroy an Egg, you must perform a Noise roll."
Based on the aforementioned underlined, I can conclude that:
- Each Melee/Shot Action, destroys 1 egg if at least 1 injury of any king is caused.
- No Contamination if you miss
- Noise roll after every single attempt.

Slightly less random & other gameplay tweaks | BoardGameGeek (https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2361400/slightly-less-random-and-other-gameplay-tweaks)
【turn416801search4】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 6.8 years ago; Crawled: last month; Nemesis is a great game, but after a few tweaks our gaming group enjoyed the game even more, making it one of our favorites. ... “Eclosion is too powerful... instead of instantly dying if you have a larvae, you just get two extra contamination” or “Consuming Fires isn’t fun... it can only add a maximum of three fires”.
I suppose taken with the other changes, it's unlikely to cause problems early, but this change just seems to run counter to your other ideas.
#7. This takes out a lot of the social element of Nemesis for me. One of the big dilemmas of the game is finding out who you can trust. This room makes sabotage very difficult to do. While this might force player-killers to be more clever and find more items or sabotage the cockpit, I think there's something missing when verification is only two cards away. Might I suggest that while you always include the Engine Control Room, maybe allow it to only check one engine per use? That way, the need to check the engines still costs far less, but the cost of complete peace of mind is still minimum four cards and will make the decision to use the ECM or make progress with one's own Objective have more consequence.
#8. This is more punishing than the current rule for getting a second Larva. I believe the current FAQ says that receiving a second Larve would only add another Contamination card. Were you not aware of this, or did you intend to make a more severe penalty?
At any rate, there are some interesting ideas here overall. Thanks for sharing!

Nemesis Review | BoardGameGeek (https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3006152/nemesis-review)
【turn416801search8】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3.8 years ago; Crawled: last month; Nemesis is a tense, claustrophobic survival game set on board a damaged space ship somewhere in the depths of space. ... This is done by bringing a dead crew member body (Either a fellow player or the body you awaken next to), an alien body, or an alien egg to the research room. ... However, by design, the game seems to want you to prefer running and evasion over direct combat, and melee combat as an absolute last resort. ... Wounds don't go into you action card deck, contamination cards do.
This unlocks three random useful bonuses such as extra damage done in combat. However, by design, the game seems to want you to prefer running and evasion over direct combat, and melee combat as an absolute last resort. Scoring hits is very hard, and scoring enough to kill the larger Aliens feels nigh impossible. While understandable, I think it leaves a bit to be desired, especially with a more combat focus class where that removes a large amount of your utility and desire to play that class. Combat is also dangerous in another way - the contamination you take from certain hits are placed into your action card deck as duds. In other words, if you would normally draw five action cards and instead draw four plus a contimation, that's just a wasted action card that turn.
Nemesis handles the gradual spiraling of events out of control very smoothly. I find the noise mechanic a little ham fisted, but also quite necessary to facilitate the other dangers that arise as the board develops. There are several key moments in the game - such as the first encounter with an Alien - that serve as a catalyst for other key events that will further shape the game.
